source_refs.note: Exercise 3.4, Question 2: Exercise 3.4, book page 94: Q1-Q15 (integration by partial fractions); answers book pages 301-302

blocks.explanation:
A proper rational function; the denominator is a quadratic that factorises.
First factorise \(x^2 + 4x + 3\), then it is Case-I (two different linear factors).
Plan: factorise, split into partial fractions, find the constants, integrate to logarithms.
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{3x + 5}{x^2 + 4x + 3}\,dx\).
To find: the integral.
Method: factorise the denominator, then partial fractions (Case-I). The fraction is proper: degree 1 < degree 2.

Write the partial fractions
\[\dfrac{3x + 5}{(x + 1)(x + 3)} = \dfrac{A}{x + 1} + \dfrac{B}{x + 3}\]
\[3x + 5 = A(x + 3) + B(x + 1) \quad (1)\]
Why: One constant over each linear factor; then multiply by \((x + 1)(x + 3)\).

Put \(x = -1\) and \(x = -3\) in (1)
\[x = -1:\ 2 = 2A,\ A = 1\]
\[x = -3:\ -4 = -2B,\ B = 2\]
Why: Each root removes one of the two terms.

Check
\[\dfrac{1}{x + 1} + \dfrac{2}{x + 3} = \dfrac{x + 3 + 2x + 2}{(x + 1)(x + 3)}\]
\[= \dfrac{3x + 5}{x^2 + 4x + 3} \;\checkmark\]
Why: The partial fractions add back to the integrand.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: In the answers at the end of the book (page 301), the answers of Exercise 3.4 are printed under the wrong heading "Exercise 3.6". The answer of this question is item (ii) of that block: \(\ln|x + 1| + 2\ln|x + 3| + c\). That answer is correct. The block headed "Exercise 3.4" (page 301) belongs to a different exercise.
